clue.text: Returning us on launch across lake? Unfortunately not!

indicators.note: returning tells us the words us and on are read back to front together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: across says one piece lies over the other, so the lake sits inside the launch

parts.note: to launch something is to chuck or throw it
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to launch a boat back over a lake is told it will not happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' hints at a trip that never happens; 'launch' is a verb (to throw), not a boat, and the lake goes inside it, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic exclamation of regret meaning that a hoped-for outcome is, sadly, not available.

clue.text: Steal, hence arrest and prison

definitions.meaning: informal British for to pinch something
informal British for to catch a criminal
British slang for a jail or police station

explanation.surface: A thief takes something and is consequently caught and locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses one word for pinching, collaring a suspect and the police cells.

clue.text: Christmas present he dreamed about, amongst others

definitions.text: Christmas present he dreamed about, amongst others

parts.words: Christmas present he dreamed about, amongst others
parts.note: in Dickens's A Christmas Carol the miser dreams of the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come

explanation.surface: Someone dreamt of a particular Christmas gift along with other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas present' reads as a gift but is the Ghost of Christmas Present.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser is visited in the night by ghosts including the Ghost of Christmas Present.

clue.text: Present deliverer of Queen's seasonal message

definitions.meaning: a Christmas gift, in Britain a tip given to tradesmen
the television set, informally a box, on which the monarch's Christmas broadcast is watched

explanation.surface: A gift brings the monarch's Christmas speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Christmas Day speech is a British television tradition; the 'box' is the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasonal gratuity or gift; also jokingly the television that carries the royal broadcast.

clue.text: 50 people employed as apprentices

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
people in work are wage earners

explanation.surface: Fifty workers are taken on as trainees.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainees picking up a trade are still acquiring their skills.

clue.text: Provides comfort for so long!

explanation.surface: A friend offers solace before saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladdens someone's spirits; and in British usage an informal goodbye or thanks.

clue.text: Starts off Christmas holiday in carefree style

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words are taken, one initial from each

explanation.surface: Someone begins a Christmas holiday feeling relaxed and fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant fashionable flair is what both words name, used as a noun.

clue.text: Supporter turns up in time to provide protection

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the next

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A backer appears just in time to shield someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'turns up' reads the supporter from the bottom upwards; 'Supporter' is the undergarment, not a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelter or give refuge, as a port shelters ships.

clue.text: Girl of 23 who found happiness in fitting success

definitions.meaning: the heroine of a classic Christmas pantomime, the answer at 23

definitions.text: who found happiness in fitting success
definitions.meaning: her glass slipper fitted, and she married the prince

explanation.surface: A girl from the show found joy when something fitted well.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine is identified by the slipper fitting her foot, then marries the prince.

clue.text: Old computer equipment involved with Christmas post?

definitions.meaning: an early machine that fed punched cards into a computer
someone busy reading the greetings cards that arrive in the December mail

explanation.surface: A piece of outdated hardware is somehow mixed up with the festive mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Punched-card input devices were standard early computing hardware; jokingly, a person reading greetings cards fits too.

clue.text: Look around St. Paul's for his monument

definitions.text: Look around St. Paul's for his monument

parts.words: Look around St. Paul's for his monument
parts.note: echoes the Latin epitaph in the cathedral for its architect: if you seek his monument, look around you

explanation.surface: Visitors to the London cathedral are told to look about them to find a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The architect of St Paul's Cathedral in London is buried there under the inscription 'Si monumentum requiris, circumspice': the building itself is his monument.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect who designed St Paul's has the whole cathedral as his memorial.

clue.text: Christmas travellers ordered new Times here

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of the following three words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Festive travellers asked for a fresh copy of The Times delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing an order with a newsagent; it rearranges NEW TIMES HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi journeyed to Bethlehem following the star, bearing gifts.

clue.text: Too wise, so to speak, for such trifles?

indicators.note: so to speak says the words before are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: said quickly, this pair of words runs together into the sound of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being overly clever rules out frivolous playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifles are small things of little value, as are playthings for children.

clue.text: Extremely mundane source of present-day deliveries?

definitions.text: Extremely mundane source of present-day deliveries?

parts.words: Extremely mundane source of present-day deliveries?
parts.note: mundane in its old sense of worldly: the place at the very top of the world, from which Santa delivers presents on Christmas Day

explanation.surface: A dull, ordinary depot dispatches modern parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mundane' looks like 'boring' but means 'of the world', so 'extremely mundane' is at the world's extremity; 'present-day' means Christmas Day, when presents arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's legendary workshop sits at the earth's northern extremity, from where he delivers Christmas gifts.

clue.text: Great excitement as filly constantly leads the field

indicators.note: leads says the earlier pieces go in front of the next

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for filly in racing form
ever means always or constantly
a pitch is a playing field

explanation.surface: Racegoers grow wild as a young mare stays at the front throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing picture misleads: 'the field' is a sports pitch, not the runners in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic for an intense state of agitation or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Remove broadcast involving Queen indefinitely?

indicators.note: involving says the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the word before are strewn into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone wants the Queen's broadcast taken off the air permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like the Queen's Christmas speech, but it is the anagram signal for 'Remove'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean for all time, without any end.

clue.text: Order initiating first Christmas journey

definitions.meaning: in Luke's gospel, the edict from Caesar Augustus for a census sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem

explanation.surface: An instruction set off the journey of the first Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order, and Caesar's census edict began the Nativity journey.

clue.text: Like some Christmas post, not directed across the ocean?

definitions.meaning: greetings cards were once sent in unstuck envelopes at a cheaper rate

explanation.surface: Some festive mail never gets shipped overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, cards in unstuck envelopes once went at a cheaper postal rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Envelopes left open, and whimsically split as never steered over the sea.

clue.text: Too much a feature of Christmas festivities?

definitions.meaning: an amount beyond what is needed
overindulgence in food and drink typifies the season

explanation.surface: Overdoing things is part and parcel of the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Surplus beyond what is reasonable, the overindulgence typical of seasonal celebrations.

clue.text: Christmas lights are capable of transforming 25

parts.note: can means are able to

indicators.note: transforming means changing the form, so the letters of the cross-referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: the answer at 25 down, a sledge

explanation.surface: Festive illuminations can change the look of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapers lit in windows and churches are traditional seasonal illuminations.

clue.text: Author seen at dance that's thrown in winter

parts.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A writer is spotted at a dance held during winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed sphere of frozen flakes is the classic missile of winter games.

clue.text: A small number in the opera

definitions.text: A small number in the opera

parts.words: A small number in the opera
parts.note: number as a musical piece: a short song in an opera

explanation.surface: Only a few people are in the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a quantity but means a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A short aria, a brief solo song within an operatic work.

clue.text: Girl's two letters lost by Santa Claus?

definitions.note: read as Girl is, the possessive standing for the verb

indicators.note: lost by says the named letters are removed from what follows

parts.note: Santa Claus is Saint Nicholas
the two letters dropped are H and S

explanation.surface: A girl's pair of letters to Father Christmas went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H and S from NICHOLAS leaves the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, the feminine form linked to Nicholas.

clue.text: Cast Emma in top festive entertainment

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded afresh, so the letters of the next three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Emma is given the starring role in the Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like casting an actor, but it signals the anagram of EMMA IN TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas theatre show with slapstick and audience participation is a British festive tradition.

clue.text: Travels over snow, taking some risk, I suppose

indicators.note: taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone crossing snow accepts that there is an element of danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding on runners across snow is what a skier does with the verb.

clue.text: With onset of snow, blazed a trail in this?

definitions.text: With onset of snow, blazed a trail in this?

indicators.note: onset of means the very start of the word that follows

parts.note: to blaze a trail is to lead the way

explanation.surface: When the snow came, someone pioneered a route on runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner-borne vehicle for travelling over snow, the kind that leads the way in winter.

clue.text: Rang bells, say, as instructed

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the phrase before is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to ring bells slowly is to toll them

explanation.surface: Someone rang the bells because they were ordered to.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered or directed to do something, past tense.

clue.text: Gold, for example, from generous first of magi — and the rest follow

parts.note: noble can mean magnanimous or generous

indicators.note: first of says to take the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: et al. is the Latin abbreviation for and the others

explanation.surface: Gold was among the gifts the first wise man brought, and the other two followed suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is a classic example of a precious metal resistant to corrosion.

clue.text: Fire-fighting equipment you may put near fire soon

definitions.meaning: a flexible pipe for spraying water

definitions.text: you may put near fire soon
definitions.meaning: stockings hung by the fireplace on Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: Gear for putting out fires is something you will soon place beside the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Firemen's flexible pipes; and hosiery, the stockings hung by the hearth for Santa.

clue.text: Closely associated with workers outside home

indicators.note: outside says the workers stand round the next piece

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, and two of them are taken
a hand is a manual worker, and two of them are taken
in means at home

explanation.surface: Labourers stand outside a house and are closely linked with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' gives two HANDs, and 'outside' puts them round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, to work together intimately, as if holding each other's hands.
